objective: Measure the bounded recall-response and Continuous Cognition contracts on synthetic baseline and holdout cases without treating contract quality as independently verified Utility.

fixture_contract.split_policy: disjoint synthetic baseline and holdout; not preregistered before the production response implementation

continuous_cognition_operation_contract_.runtime_proof: Go route and native CLI tests exercise every operation; this offline matrix proves deterministic contract shape without claiming external execution.

continuous_cognition.evidence_basis: synthetic contract-regression projection plus deterministic Go lifecycle tests

independent_utility.reason: Offline response quality and observed utility are not independently reconciled proof of causal benefit.

failures.meaning: The implementation and synthetic contract evaluation do not manufacture an independently verified or causal product-effect claim.

limitations: Fixtures contain synthetic opaque references only; they do not measure live retrieval or model-generated answer quality.
The holdout is structurally disjoint but was not preregistered before the production response implementation, so it is contract-regression evidence rather than an unbiased product-effect estimate.
The static response condition is a deterministic contract projection and does not prove production correctness, currentness, or utility.
Advisory abstention remains the safe action posture until exact independent verification and causal Utility evidence exist.
Latency and token counts are unmeasured in this offline harness (null); tool calls and failures are exact harness counts, while privacy and determinism are contract checks, not production telemetry.
Continuous Cognition is implemented and contract-tested here, but this synthetic projection does not establish live model quality, latency, token cost, independent Utility, or causal product lift.
